Measuring cream cheese

A cup of cream cheese weighs about 227 g, and you rarely need to measure it, because a standard 8 oz block is exactly that: 226.8 g, which fills about one cup. Two blocks make 2 cups (454 g), the amount in a lot of cheesecake recipes.

Cream cheese is too stiff to measure accurately in a cup. It traps air pockets and smears up the sides. Go by the block, or use the markings on the foil wrapper, which usually show tablespoon lines (1 tablespoon is about 14 g).

Whipped cream cheese in a tub has air beaten into it, so a cup weighs noticeably less. Don't swap it cup for cup into baking recipes; weigh it instead.

Source: US packaging: one 8 oz block = 226.8 g and fills about 1 cup; King Arthur Baking lists 1 cup = 227 g.

Questions

How many grams is ½ cup of cream cheese?

½ cup of cream cheese weighs about 114 g (4 oz). A full cup is 227 g.

How many cups is 100 grams of cream cheese?

100 g of cream cheese is about ½ cup, based on 227 g per cup.

How many cups is an 8 oz block of cream cheese?

About 1 cup. An 8 oz block weighs 226.8 g, which is the weight of 1 cup of cream cheese.
